name: Eber
overview: Eber is a male member of the tribe of Levi, uniquely identified as the son of Amok according to Nehemiah 12:20. He is noted among the descendants of Aaron, who served as priests. His lineage places him within the priestly heritage of Israel, emphasizing his role within the Levitical priesthood.
namesAndTitles: The name Eber means "[regions] beyond [the river]," reflecting a geographical or ancestral significance. This proper name, as recorded in Nehemiah 12:20, is not indicated as being given directly by God but carries a meaningful designation linked to his identity.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records that Eber is the son of Amok, as stated in Nehemiah 12:20. Beyond this, no additional family relationships are detailed in the provided data.
scriptureSignificance: Eber holds an important place in the biblical narrative as a link in the Levitical priestly line descending from Aaron, underscoring the continuity of God’s appointed priesthood. Additionally, he is recognized as an ancestor in the godly lineage that leads to Abraham, marking him as a foundational figure in the preservation of God’s covenant people after the flood. His name also serves as the root for the term 'Hebrew,' identifying the people of God in Scripture.
